speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are pregnant and suffering from fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise; how many weeks pregnant are you and when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. The consumption of ice cream three days prior is a key clue. To confirm my suspicion, can you describe the texture of the ice cream (specifically if it was soft-serve with visible ribbons) and whether anyone else who ate it is also feeling ill? text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever. I also have Headache, Anorexia, Fatigue, Malaise. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning, as iron deficiency anemia does not typically cause fever, anorexia, or sudden malaise in this manner. Given your specific history of eating soft-serve ice cream with ribbons and the sudden onset of these symptoms, can you tell me exactly how high your fever is and whether you have noticed any muscle aches or a stiff neck? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Differential; REQUEST TEST: Peripheral Blood Smear.

text: The CBC shows leukocytosis with a normal hemoglobin level, which contradicts the previous suggestion of iron deficiency anemia. While the smear report is negative for inclusions, the clinical picture of sudden fever, headache, and the specific consumption of soft-serve ice cream raises a high suspicion for Listeriosis. Is your headache severe, and have you experienced any photophobia or blurred vision? REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI.

text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. The patient is currently pregnant, at her 30th week of gestation. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travels or contact with sick individuals. No known allergies.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's history of consuming soft-serve ice cream, combined with leukocytosis and symptoms of fever, headache, and malaise at 30 weeks gestation, is highly suspicious for Listeriosis. Has she developed any neurological symptoms like confusion, seizures, or severe back pain, and is there any history of miscarriage or preterm labor?
